Joburg Burn

By: Johann Botha | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Gauteng is burning as thousands of citizens take to the streets to protest the lack of service delivery...

Press Release:


Service delivery protests
From looting shops and burning a truck in Eldarado Park to violent altercations with police in Ennerdale, Gauteng is in the grip of service delivery protests. But why has the
provincial government failed to respond to the plight of the poor? Carte Blanche examines the issues

Script:


Aki Anastasio

link
Driving to work we regularly hear traffic reports that warn us about stationery vehicles, broken down cars, traffic lights that are not working and protest action. Protest action and violent ones are becoming a regular occurrence in South Africa, but people don't just protest fro no reason.

Monday's protests started in Ennerdale, and quickly spread to Eldorado Park, Freedom Park, Kliptown, Orange Farm, Lenasia, Finetown and other areas Sout West of Joburg - with running battles ensuing between stone throwing protestors and public order police firing rubber bullets.
PAC man
Since yesterday we are waiting for the government officials and the mayor of the DA. They don't come. And this riot are taking out of hands now. And the police are shooting our people with right bullets. And we feel that is totally wrong.

This little shop was burnt down on Wednesday morning- The owner, who for religious reasons can't appear on camera, is distraught
Shop owner
This building has been here since 1960, it's been a community shop where people grew up. We help one another against fights. This was a community shop.

The speaker of the Johannesburg City Parliament, Vasco da Gama lives nearby and was WOKEN UP by the noise of the fire
Vasco
What do you do when your own children don't have housing to stay at. I really empathise with the community's plight, but let them give this new administration of the city of Johannesburg a chance to really come and deal with the issues.

The head of the Institute for Race Relations says the protests are caused by expectations created during the rainbow days of Mandela and Mbeki
Frans Cronje
The capita incomes and family living standards were increasing very rapidly, particularly between 2004 and 2007. And that trend has been broken in recent years.

Three things happened in short succession – the ousting of Thabo Mbeki, the global financial crisis and then global commodity prices were depressed.
Frans Cronje
And the combination of the three, the three waves are too much for SA economy to withstand and the growth rate struggles valiantly out of the crisis here in 2009, which was a negative growth year. It touches 3% again in 2010 and 11. But it's too much. And the pressure is on the economy and entrepreneurs and risk takers and investors are such that the growth rate gets knocked down to virtually 0% last year.

And, as the growth rate REMAINED LOW, public confidence dropped and the amount of protests started increasing..
Ruth da Costa's parents received this small 4 room house in Eldorado Park from the apartheid government 40 years ago. Today, 11 people spanning 4 generations are cramMed into the size of the average double garage in the more affluent suburbs. Only one of them is employed. Ruth supports the protests.
Ruth (AFRIKAANS)
The house we live in is too small. My eldest daughter is 28. She has 3 children. My twins they have 1 each. And then there is my brother.It is too claustrophobic. Everyone needs his privacy. We can't anymore.

Ruth was promised a RDP house in 1995. Nothing happened, and when Freedom Park was built 10 years later she once again put her name down in vain.
Ruth (AFRIKAANS)
Once the houses were completed the people didn't come back to us. Then we saw there were other people in the houses. And we're still standing right where we are.

Government blames the global recession, yet other developing countries have already recovered
Frans
SA's economic growth rate has peeled away downwards as the rest of the world recovered out of the global financial crisis in 2009. The problem is not with South Africa's people and their expectations. The problem lies with the South African economy that can no longer meet the very reasonable expectations, even very patient expectations that were created in the first 15 years after 1994.

Joburg mayor Herman Mashaba agrees
herman
If you look at the performance of most of the countries in the world, unfortunately South Africa is failing. Honestly let us not fool ourselves that is because of global economic challenges. South Africa's problems are self-inflicted.

The DA has been in power for 9 months but MASHABA SAYS they're still working under the ANC budget they inherited – which was totally inadequate to address the problem.
Herman
I'm appealing to our residents; please don't expect me to address a R170b infrastructure backlog in 9 months with only R10b available to do it.

The new administration's first budget will be presented this month, but they will still be dependant on the national government for the money they need. Which is why they are trying to lure international investors to the city
Herman
As long as the economy of this country does not perform, we've got a crisis.

At Tuesday's community meeting councilor da Gama asked the residents for 2 weeks to come up with a plan
vasco
The executive mayor and his team will come out in the next two weeks to address all the issues that they've mentioned so that we can get a way forward, take the community with us in the service delivery problems that they've described.

This calmed RESIDENTS down, but after the meeting, when they were walking home, Ruth says the police started firing on them for no apparent reason
Ruth (AFRIKAANS)
As they started shooting at us I was the last one that could get away because all the kids shoved the adults out of the way so they can get away. As I ran I thought I was going to get a bullet. And it was just like that and I felt the bullet in my spine.

On Wednesday morning the streets were burning again
Ruth
I have very little faith in the government, especially when it comes to Eldorado Park, I do not believe.

Frans says that the amount of eligible voters who did not vote in the last elections outnumber the voters who voted in favour of the ANC, and non-voting is not due to apathy
Frans
We know who that person typically is. He's a young South African, better educated than his parents, higher standard of living. Most probably unemployed with great hopes for his future that he cannot possibly meet. And when he looks across the political spectrum from the one extreme to the other there's no party that could stand in front of that young man and say to him “If you vote for me the policies that we will introduce I guarantee you will meet your expectations for a better life”. And so that young man turns to protest action.
Mayor
Protesting is part and parcel of a democratic system. So we need to encourage our people to engage because such engagement actually gets the attention of politicians.

By the end of the week all the politicians had visited the area, more promises were made and committees formed. And more than 70 people had been arrested
Frans
We're not on the verge of a revolution. What they are is the warning that if we do not take seriously the disappointment of large numbers of young people we will have the revolution in the decade ahead.




PROMO 15”
South Africa is fast earning a reputation as the protest capital of the world...

“...”

Protests, an irritating past of the daily traffic report or a serious threat tot he country?
